experiences.name: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore the stunning La Jolla Cove with the family. Snorkel among colorful fish and sea lions in the protected marine reserve, then relax on the sandy beach. Kids love spotting seals and sea lions sunbathing on the rocks nearby at Children's Pool.

experiences.name: San Diego Zoo Visit
experiences.description: One of the world's most famous zoos, home to over 3,500 animals across 650 species. Kids and adults alike will love the giant pandas, giraffes, and the Africa Rocks exhibit. The guided bus tour is a great way to cover the expansive grounds with young children.

experiences.name: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon on one of America's most beautiful beaches, consistently ranked in the top 10 nationally. Build sandcastles, swim in calm waters, and enjoy a sunset picnic near the iconic Hotel del Coronado. The wide, flat beach is perfect for families with young children.

experiences.name: Birch Aquarium at Scripps
experiences.description: An educational and entertaining aquarium experience for the whole family. Explore tide pools, watch shark feedings, and marvel at the stunning kelp forest tank. The outdoor tide pool plaza lets kids touch sea stars and sea cucumbers in a hands-on setting.
experiences.location: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, La Jolla

experiences.name: Old Town San Diego Food and Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore California's birthplace with a self-guided walking tour through historic adobe buildings and lively plazas. Sample authentic Mexican street tacos, churros, and horchata at the colorful market stalls. Visit the free State Historic Park to learn about early California life — a fun and educational experience for the whole family.
experiences.location: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park, Old Town

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - San Diego
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day
experiences.description: Explore the stunning La Jolla Cove with the family. Snorkel among colorful fish and sea lions in the protected marine reserve, then relax on the sandy beach. Kids love spotting seals and sea lions sunbathing on the rocks nearby at Children's Pool.

experiences.description: Spend an afternoon on one of America's most beautiful beaches, consistently ranked in the top 10 nationally. Build sandcastles, swim in calm waters, and enjoy a sunset picnic near the iconic Hotel del Coronado. The wide, flat beach is perfect for families with young children.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight WN lands at 12:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (take the 992 Flyer bus from the airport to downtown for ~$2.50, then connect to Mission Bay), and check in to Mission Bay Family Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk or drive to Mission Bay Park (just steps from the hotel). Let the kids splash in the calm bay waters, explore the grassy picnic areas, and enjoy the free beach access. Rent a paddleboat or kayak from Mission Bay Sportcenter (~$20/hour) if budget allows, or simply relax on the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Mission Bay boardwalk as the sun sets over the water. Head to Garnet Avenue in Pacific Beach (10-minute drive or short bus ride) for a casual family dinner. Explore the lively strip and window-shop before heading back to the hotel for an early rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before landing — budget ~$8–10 per person.
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable tacos at a local taqueria near the hotel such as Oscar's Mexican Seafood on Garnet Ave — fish tacos for ~$4–5 each.
meals.dinner: Hodad's in Ocean Beach or a nearby In-N-Out Burger for a filling, wallet-friendly family meal (~$8–12 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since travel can be tiring, especially for kids. Pre-pack snacks for the plane and airport to save money. Mission Bay Park is free and within walking distance of the resort — perfect for a low-key first afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Head to La Jolla Cove for a Snorkeling and Beach Day (drive ~20 minutes or take the 30 bus). Arrive early (8:30–9:00 AM) to grab a free parking spot or street parking before crowds arrive. Rent snorkel gear from La Jolla Cove Snorkel (~$20/person) or bring your own. Swim alongside sea lions, colorful fish, and leopard sharks in the protected cove — an unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, walk along the La Jolla Cove trail to Children's Pool Beach to spot harbor seals lounging on the sand. Explore the free Birch Aquarium at Scripps Institution of Oceanography nearby (~$21 adults, ~$14 kids — book online for discounts). Enjoy the tide pools and ocean exhibits with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus back toward Mission Bay. Stop at Sunset Cliffs Natural Park in Ocean Beach for a stunning free sunset view over the Pacific. Then head to Ocean Beach for dinner on Newport Avenue before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab grocery-store items the night before (cereal, fruit, yogurt) and eat at the hotel to save money — budget ~$3–5 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at La Jolla Cove — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks from a nearby Ralph's or Vons supermarket (~$5–7 per person).
meals.dinner: Ortega's Cocina in Ocean Beach for affordable, authentic Mexican food — plates run ~$10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: La Jolla Cove is one of San Diego's top free beaches. Snorkeling is best in the morning when water is calmer and visibility is clearest. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes, and towels. The bus route 30 connects Mission Bay to La Jolla — check the MTS app for schedules (~$2.50/ride).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Balboa Park — San Diego's crown jewel of free outdoor space. Explore the beautiful Spanish Colonial architecture, lush gardens, and free outdoor attractions. Many of the park's museums offer free admission on rotating Tuesdays (check the Balboa Park free Tuesday schedule in advance). Walk the El Prado promenade, visit the Botanical Building and Lily Pond (free), and let kids run in the open plazas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the San Diego Zoo, located inside Balboa Park. Purchase tickets online in advance for a discount (~$62 adults, ~$52 kids 3–11; look for AAA discounts or Costco deals). The Zoo is world-class and a must-do for families. Highlights include the panda exhibit, Africa Rocks, and the Skyfari aerial tram. Plan at least 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and enjoy a relaxing evening at Mission Bay. Walk the boardwalk, watch the sunset over the bay, and let the kids wind down with a swim in the hotel pool. Keep dinner simple and close to home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local diner — try Kono's Cafe in Pacific Beach for hearty breakfast burritos (~$8–10 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and eat inside the Zoo to avoid expensive food court prices, or budget ~$12–15 per person at the Zoo's Albert's Restaurant for a sit-down meal.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries at Ralph's or Trader Joe's for a simple picnic dinner at Mission Bay Park — sandwiches, salads, and fruit (~$5–8 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Balboa Park is free to enter — only individual museums charge admission. The San Diego Zoo is a splurge but well worth it for families. Book Zoo tickets online at least a few days ahead for best prices. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll log 5–8 miles easily between the park and Zoo.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Coronado Island for a Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic day. Take the free Coronado Ferry from Broadway Pier in downtown San Diego (~$5.75 each way per person) — a fun boat ride the kids will love. Arrive at Coronado Beach, consistently ranked one of America's most beautiful beaches. Set up on the wide, white sand beach and enjoy the calm, warm surf with the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or rent bikes along the Coronado Beach boardwalk (bike rentals ~$10–15/hour from Holland's Bicycles). Explore the grounds of the iconic Hotel del Coronado — walking around the exterior and grounds is free and offers gorgeous photo opportunities. Browse the shops on Orange Avenue, Coronado's charming main street, and enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on the beach for the famous Coronado Beach sunset — the sky turns brilliant shades of orange and pink over the Pacific. Enjoy your pre-packed picnic dinner on the beach as the sun dips below the horizon. Take the ferry back to downtown and then bus or rideshare back to Mission Bay.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab pastries and coffee from a local bakery before heading to the ferry — budget ~$5–8 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on Coronado Beach — sandwiches, chips, fruit, and drinks from a grocery store (~$5–7 per person). Saves significantly vs. beachside restaurants.
meals.dinner: Picnic dinner on the beach at sunset (pack from the hotel or a grocery store — ~$6–8 per person) OR grab a budget meal at Miguel's Cocina on Orange Avenue (~$12–15 per person) before the ferry back.

day_by_day.notes: The Coronado Ferry departs from Broadway Pier (downtown) approximately every hour. Factor in travel time — plan to leave the hotel by 9:00 AM to make the most of the day. Coronado Beach is ideal for young children due to its wide, flat shoreline and relatively calm waves. Bring beach toys, sunscreen, and extra towels.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning at Pacific Beach (PB) — just a short walk or drive from Mission Bay Family Resort. Enjoy a leisurely walk along the Pacific Beach Boardwalk (Crystal Pier to Mission Beach), one of San Diego's most iconic beach promenades. Watch surfers, browse the eclectic shops, and soak up the Southern California beach culture one last time. Let the kids play in the waves for a final swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit SeaWorld San Diego if budget allows (~$75–90/person, but check for online deals, military discounts, or last-minute offers that can drop prices significantly). Alternatively, for a free option, explore Tecolote Shores and Fiesta Island at Mission Bay — a beautiful, uncrowded area perfect for a final afternoon of paddling, kite flying, or picnicking with bay views. Check out and store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Mission Beach or Pacific Beach area before heading to the airport. San Diego International Airport (SAN) is only 10–15 minutes from Mission Bay — take the 992 Flyer bus back (~$2.50) or arrange a rideshare. Reflect on a wonderful budget-friendly San Diego family vacation!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or splurge on a sit-down meal at Broken Yolk Cafe in Pacific Beach — a beloved local breakfast spot (~$12–15 per person, portions are huge).
meals.lunch: Grab fish tacos at World Famous restaurant on Pacific Beach or Rubio's Coastal Grill for affordable, classic San Diego fare (~$8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Filippi's Pizza Grotto in Pacific Beach — a San Diego institution with generous, affordable Italian food (~$10–14 per person) before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Leave extra time to get to the airport during August — summer traffic near the beaches can be heavy. Keep a small emergency budget buffer (~$50–75) for unexpected costs like parking, tips, or last-minute souvenirs. Total estimated daily budget per family of 4: ~$120–180/day excluding hotel and major attractions.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight WN arrives at 12:00 PM. Travel from the airport to Mission Bay Family Resort, check in, and get settled. Freshen up and orient the family with the resort amenities and nearby surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mission Bay Park on foot or rent bikes/surrey bikes near the resort. Enjoy the calm bay waters, grassy picnic areas, and playgrounds. Let the kids splash in the bay's gentle shores to kick off the beach vibe without overcommitting on the first day.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Mission Bay boardwalk at sunset, then head to a casual nearby dinner spot to relax after travel.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick and easy bite near the airport or pick up sandwiches and snacks at a nearby grocery store (e.g., Vons or Trader Joe's on Mission Bay Drive) to eat at the resort upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Eat at Firefly Eatery & Bar or The Atoll Restaurant at the resort for a convenient, relaxed first-night dinner. Expect mid-range pricing (~$15–$25 per adult entrée). Kid-friendly menu available.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and low-key. Prioritize unpacking, hydrating, and adjusting to the San Diego timezone. Apply sunscreen generously – August in San Diego means strong UV rays even on overcast 'June Gloom' days, which can linger into August mornings.

day_by_day.morning: San Diego Zoo Visit – Head to Balboa Park early (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the midday heat. Spend the morning exploring iconic exhibits like the Africa Rocks, Elephant Odyssey, and the Children's Zoo. Use the Skyfari aerial tram for a bird's-eye view of the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the San Diego Zoo through the afternoon, focusing on the Giant Panda exhibit and Polar Bear Plunge. Take a guided bus tour of the zoo to cover more ground with kids. Grab lunch inside the zoo at one of several mid-range dining options.
day_by_day.evening: After the zoo, drive through Balboa Park and admire the Spanish Colonial architecture. Head back toward Mission Bay for a relaxed evening at the resort pool or bay beach.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at the resort or grab pastries and coffee at a local café such as Better Buzz Coffee (multiple locations) before heading out.
meals.lunch: Eat inside the San Diego Zoo at Albert's Restaurant or Treetops Café – mid-range options with burgers, salads, and kid-friendly meals (~$12–$20 per person). Alternatively, pack a light snack bag to supplement.
meals.dinner: Visit Rubio's Coastal Grill near Mission Bay for casual, affordable fish tacos and burritos – a San Diego staple (~$10–$15 per person). Great for families after a long zoo day.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase San Diego Zoo tickets online in advance to save time and potentially money. Arrive right at opening (9:00 AM) to see the most active animals and avoid peak afternoon heat. Bring a stroller for young children – the zoo covers significant ground. Comfortable walking shoes are a must.

day_by_day.morning: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day – Drive approximately 20 minutes north to La Jolla Cove. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to secure parking and a good spot on the beach. Rent snorkel gear from La Jolla Water Sports or bring your own. Snorkel among garibaldi fish, leopard sharks, and playful sea lions in the protected cove waters. The underwater visibility is typically excellent in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, walk the La Jolla Cove trail to the Children's Pool (a sheltered beach with harbor seals) and enjoy the scenic coastal bluffs. Browse the charming shops and galleries along Prospect Street in La Jolla Village. Let the kids play on the beach while adults relax.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the La Jolla coastline, then head into La Jolla Village for dinner before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Fuel up before snorkeling at The Cottage La Jolla – a beloved local breakfast spot with hearty omelets, pancakes, and fresh fruit (~$12–$18 per person). Arrive early as it gets busy.
meals.lunch: Pick up fish tacos, wraps, or acai bowls from a beachside café or food truck near La Jolla Cove. Puesto La Jolla offers excellent upscale-casual Mexican food (~$15–$22 per person).
meals.dinner: Dine at Zenbu Sushi Bar & Restaurant in La Jolla for fresh, mid-range sushi and Japanese fare (~$20–$35 per person). Alternatively, try The Promiscuous Fork for creative, family-friendly dishes at a lower price point.

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling at La Jolla Cove is best at high tide for clearer water and more marine life. Check tide charts before going. Sea lions are commonly spotted and are entertaining but should not be approached. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only – La Jolla Cove is a protected marine reserve. Parking can be competitive; consider arriving before 9:00 AM or using a paid lot on Prospect Street.

day_by_day.morning: Birch Aquarium at Scripps – Located in La Jolla (about 20 minutes from the resort), this world-class aquarium opens at 9:00 AM. Explore the Hall of Fishes featuring Pacific and tropical marine life, the giant kelp forest tank, and the seahorse exhibit. Kids will love the hands-on tide pool plaza where they can touch sea stars and hermit crabs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Town San Diego Food and Culture Tour – Drive to Old Town San Diego State Historic Park (about 20 minutes from La Jolla). Take a self-guided walking tour through historic adobe buildings, the Whaley House (one of America's most haunted), Seeley Stables, and the free museums. Sample authentic Mexican food and browse artisan shops and folk art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mission Bay and enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort. Take advantage of the resort's pool, lawn games, or evening programming for families.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the resort's café or stop at Panera Bread or a local bagel shop en route to the aquarium to keep costs low and timing flexible.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch in Old Town San Diego at Casa Guadalajara – a festive, family-friendly Mexican restaurant with a large outdoor patio, mariachi music, and authentic dishes (~$14–$22 per person). Kids love the atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Enjoy a casual dinner at the resort or order takeout from a nearby Mission Bay spot. Try Saska's Steaks and Seafood on Mission Blvd for a classic San Diego dining experience (~$20–$30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Birch Aquarium offers a 'Tide Pool Cart' experience on weekends – check the schedule in advance. Old Town San Diego is entirely free to explore; only some museum exhibits charge a small fee. The Old Town Farmers Market runs on Saturdays if your visit aligns. Wear comfortable shoes for Old Town's cobblestone paths. August afternoons in Old Town can be warm – carry water bottles.

day_by_day.morning: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic – Start the final morning with a trip to Coronado Island via the scenic Coronado Bridge (about 20 minutes from the resort). Arrive at Coronado Beach, consistently ranked among America's most beautiful, and spend the morning swimming, building sandcastles, and soaking up the iconic views of the Hotel del Coronado. The wide, white-sand beach is perfect for a leisurely final-morning family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Coronado's charming Orange Avenue for boutique shopping and ice cream. Visit the historic Hotel del Coronado lobby and grounds (free to walk through). Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach or in Coronado's Centennial Park. Begin heading back to the resort in the mid-to-late afternoon to pack up and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner near Mission Bay or in the Gaslamp Quarter (if time allows before any evening flights or early next-day travel). Reflect on the trip and enjoy one last San Diego sunset.

meals.breakfast: Pick up pastries, fresh fruit, and coffee from the Coronado Ferry Landing Marketplace or a local café on Orange Avenue such as Café 1134 – a Coronado classic with great omelets and pancakes (~$10–$16 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a Coronado deli or Sprouts Farmers Market for a budget-friendly, relaxed beach lunch. Alternatively, grab fish and chips at Clayton's Coffee Shop (~$12–$18 per person) for a retro diner experience.
meals.dinner: Celebrate the final night at Ketch Grill & Taps in Mission Bay or Bali Hai Restaurant on Shelter Island for waterfront dining with stunning bay views and a festive atmosphere (~$20–$35 per person). Kid-friendly menus available.

day_by_day.notes: Coronado Beach faces west-southwest, making it one of the best spots in San Diego for a sunset view – if your schedule allows, linger until golden hour. The Hotel del Coronado is a National Historic Landmark and worth a brief self-guided tour of the lobby and grounds at no cost. If traveling back to the airport on this day, allow 30–45 minutes from Coronado or Mission Bay to San Diego International Airport (SAN). Return any rental equipment and double-check checkout time with the resort.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Flight WN arrives at 12:00 PM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect luggage and arrange private car transfer to Mission Bay Family Resort. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodations overlooking Mission Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the Mission Bay shoreline directly accessible from the resort. Rent paddleboards or kayaks from the resort's water sports center for a relaxed introduction to San Diego's stunning waterways. Let the kids splash in the calm bay waters while adults unwind on the private beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at The Shores Restaurant at La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club — a beloved San Diego institution offering oceanfront dining with fresh Pacific seafood. Enjoy sunset views over the water as you toast to the start of your trip. Alternatively, dine at Catamaran Resort's Oceana Coastal Kitchen for a convenient, upscale meal just minutes from Mission Bay Resort.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a light meal at the airport before landing — consider the airport's premium lounges if available.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual but quality bite near the resort upon arrival — try World Famous restaurant on Mission Beach for fresh fish tacos and coastal California cuisine.
meals.dinner: The Shores Restaurant at La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club — upscale Pacific Rim and California cuisine with unobstructed ocean views. Reserve a window table in advance. Budget approximately $80–$120 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury car or SUV transfer from San Diego International Airport to Mission Bay Resort for a seamless arrival experience. Contact the resort concierge in advance to arrange early check-in if possible, as the flight lands at noon. Ask the concierge to pre-stock the suite with snacks, beverages, and any family essentials.

day_by_day.morning: La Jolla Cove Snorkeling and Beach Day — Head to the iconic La Jolla Cove, just a 15-minute drive from Mission Bay. Arrange a private guided snorkeling tour for the family through a premium outfitter such as La Jolla Kayak or Everyday California. Swim alongside playful sea lions, garibaldi fish, and colorful marine life in the crystal-clear protected cove waters. Younger children can explore the shoreline tide pools while older family members snorkel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying La Jolla — walk along Prospect Street, San Diego's Riviera-style luxury shopping and dining corridor. Browse boutiques and galleries, then relax at the Children's Pool beach nearby. Consider visiting the La Jolla Cave Store and taking the staircase down to Sunny Jim's Sea Cave for a unique geological experience the whole family will love.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at George's at the Cove in La Jolla — one of San Diego's most celebrated fine dining destinations. Choose the Ocean Terrace rooftop for casual elegance with sweeping Pacific views, or the California Modern dining room for an award-winning tasting menu experience. Finish the evening with a gelato stroll along Prospect Street before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or resort restaurant — order a full family breakfast with fresh fruit, eggs, and pastries. Many luxury resorts offer in-suite dining; confirm with Mission Bay Resort concierge.
meals.lunch: The Marine Room or a beachside café in La Jolla — try Brockton Villa for brunch-style lunch on the cliffs above La Jolla Cove with spectacular views.
meals.dinner: George's at the Cove, La Jolla — California Modern cuisine with panoramic ocean views. Reserve well in advance. Budget $100–$150 per adult for the full experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling tour at least 2–3 days in advance through Everyday California or La Jolla Kayak. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, rash guards for the kids, and water shoes for the rocky tide pool areas. August water temperatures in La Jolla average 68–72°F — wetsuits may be provided by the tour operator but confirm ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: San Diego Zoo Visit — Arrive at opening time (typically 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds at one of the world's premier zoological parks. Purchase premium Backstage Pass or VIP guided tour packages for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience with animal keepers. Highlights include the Giant Panda exhibit, Africa Rocks, Elephant Odyssey, and the Skyfari Aerial Tram. The zoo is approximately 20 minutes from Mission Bay by car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the San Diego Zoo through the afternoon — with over 100 acres, a full day is easily spent here. Take the Guided Bus Tour for a comprehensive overview, then revisit favorite animal habitats. Visit the Children's Zoo section for interactive animal encounters perfect for younger family members. The zoo's premium dining options include Treetops Terrace with elevated views over the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Mission Bay area for a relaxed evening. Visit the Bahia Resort Hotel's Bahia Belle sternwheeler cruise on Mission Bay — a classic San Diego experience offering a scenic bay cruise at sunset. Then enjoy dinner at Firefly Eatery & Bar or head to nearby Pacific Beach for dinner at Sushi Ota, San Diego's most acclaimed Japanese restaurant, for an extraordinary omakase experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading to the zoo — opt for the resort's full-service restaurant or a quick stop at a local favorite like The Broken Yolk Café for hearty morning fuel.
meals.lunch: Treetops Terrace inside the San Diego Zoo — elevated dining with treetop views and a surprisingly solid menu of California-inspired dishes. Alternatively, pack a premium picnic prepared by the resort concierge.
meals.dinner: Sushi Ota in Pacific Beach — San Diego's most prestigious Japanese restaurant, known for exceptional omakase and traditional sushi. Reserve weeks in advance. Budget $120–$200 per adult for omakase.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase San Diego Zoo tickets online in advance and consider the Zoo + Safari Park combo pass if planning to visit the Safari Park later. The VIP Experience or Backstage Pass must be booked separately and offers extraordinary access for families. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the zoo involves significant uphill terrain. Arrive early as August is peak season and the zoo will be busy.

day_by_day.morning: Birch Aquarium at Scripps Institution of Oceanography — Located in La Jolla with stunning ocean views, this world-class aquarium offers an educational and immersive experience for the whole family. Explore the Tide Pool Plaza, the Shark Reef exhibit, and the mesmerizing seahorse gallery. Check the schedule for special feeding demonstrations and ranger-led tide pool tours. The aquarium opens at 9:00 AM and is approximately 20 minutes from Mission Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coronado Beach Sunset Picnic Afternoon — After the aquarium, drive to Coronado Island via the iconic Coronado Bridge (approximately 25 minutes). Check in for a tour of the historic Hotel del Coronado, one of America's most famous Victorian beach resorts. Arrange a premium private beach picnic through the Hotel del Coronado's catering service or bring a gourmet spread from Venissimo Cheese or Whole Foods Market. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the wide, pristine Coronado Beach — consistently ranked among America's most beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Coronado Beach sunset, often painting the sky in brilliant oranges and pinks behind the Hotel del Coronado. Enjoy dinner at 1500 OCEAN at the Hotel del Coronado — an elegant oceanfront restaurant offering California coastal cuisine with impeccable service. After dinner, take a romantic evening stroll along the Coronado Beach boardwalk before heading back to Mission Bay.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or visit Queenstown Public House in Mission Hills for a premium brunch-style morning meal with artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Light, gourmet picnic on Coronado Beach — arrange a luxury picnic basket through the Hotel del Coronado concierge featuring charcuterie, fresh sandwiches, artisan cheeses, fruit, and sparkling beverages. Perfect for the whole family.
meals.dinner: 1500 OCEAN at the Hotel del Coronado — upscale California coastal cuisine in an iconic oceanfront setting. One of San Diego's most celebrated dining experiences. Budget $90–$140 per adult. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Coronado Bridge offers spectacular views — consider arriving via San Diego Bay Ferry from Broadway Pier for a scenic water crossing the kids will love (approximately 15-minute ride). Birch Aquarium can get busy; arrive at opening time for the best experience. Bring beach toys, towels, and reef-safe sunscreen for the Coronado Beach afternoon. Confirm picnic arrangements with the Hotel del Coronado catering team 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Old Town San Diego Food and Culture Tour — Begin your final full day with a self-guided or private guided walking tour through Old Town San Diego State Historic Park, California's birthplace. Explore authentic adobe buildings, the Whaley House (one of America's most haunted), the Wells Fargo History Museum, and vibrant Mexican-California heritage sites. Hire a private local historian guide through Viator or GetYourGuide for an enriched family experience with storytelling tailored to all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mission Bay for a farewell afternoon of water activities — book a private luxury boat charter on Mission Bay or San Diego Bay for 2–3 hours. Options include a sailing catamaran, a pontoon party boat, or a luxury yacht charter through companies like Seaforth Boat Rentals or Gone Sailing Adventures. Enjoy the sparkling bay waters, spot wildlife, and take in the San Diego skyline from the water. Alternatively, return to a favorite beach spot for one last relaxed afternoon in the California sun.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Addison at The Grand Del Mar — San Diego's only Forbes Five-Star restaurant, offering a spectacular French-inspired tasting menu in an opulent Mediterranean-style estate setting. This is the pinnacle of San Diego fine dining and the perfect way to conclude a luxury family trip. After dinner, return to the resort for a final evening and begin packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Splurge on a full resort breakfast — order room service or dine at the resort restaurant with the full spread. Enjoy the Mission Bay views one last time over coffee and a leisurely morning meal.
meals.lunch: Old Town Mexican Café or Casa de Reyes in Old Town San Diego — both offer authentic, vibrant Mexican cuisine in the heart of historic Old Town. Try handmade tortillas, carnitas, and fresh guacamole. Festive and family-friendly.
meals.dinner: Addison at The Grand Del Mar — San Diego's crown jewel of fine dining. Multi-course French-California tasting menu with world-class wine pairings. Reserve weeks in advance. Budget $250–$350 per adult. A truly unforgettable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: If departing on Day 6, arrange a private car transfer from Mission Bay Resort to San Diego International Airport the following morning. Confirm checkout time with the resort and request late checkout if needed. Keep the final afternoon flexible — if the family wants more beach time or to revisit a favorite spot, adjust accordingly. Consider purchasing San Diego souvenirs in Old Town during the morning tour. Addison requires smart casual to formal attire; plan outfits accordingly.
